seoTitle: Mahón cruise port guide: Moll de Ponent, steps and lift
seoDescription: Ships dock below Maó; the old town is about 650 m up 100-plus steps or a 25 m lift. Museu de Menorca €4 (2026). Punta Prima beach is 10 km by taxi or bus.
quickAnswer: Ships dock at the harbour quays directly below Maó, mostly on the Moll de Ponent, so you walk into town. The old town sits about 25–30 m above the water: climb the 100-plus steps of the Costa de ses Voltes, about 650 m to Plaça de la Conquesta, or take the lift up to the Claustre del Carme. Be back at the ship 60 minutes before all-aboard.
intro: Mahón, Maó in Catalan, is Menorca's capital, built on a cliff above one of the largest natural harbours in the Mediterranean. Ships sail about 5 km up the narrow channel past the Lazareto and Quarantine islands and tie up right under the town, so the day starts on foot. The only obstacle is the climb: a stone staircase or a lift takes you up to a compact old town of churches, markets and Georgian-era houses from the British period. Beaches on the south and north-east coasts are 15 minutes or so by taxi, and the far end of the island, Ciutadella, is a 45 km trip.

terminals.name: Moll de Ponent cruise quay and maritime station
terminals.notes: Main cruise quay below the old town, with a cruise maritime station (Ports de Balears put a ground-floor refurbishment out to tender in 2024), taxis and coach parking. The port can take three cruise ships at once. The Xoriguer gin distillery is on the Moll de Ponent a short walk from the ships. About 650 m to Plaça de la Conquesta via the Costa de ses Voltes steps.

terminals.name: Cos Nou
terminals.notes: Overflow quay, used occasionally for smaller ships or when the main quay is full. About a 20-minute walk to town.

walkability.detail: From the Moll de Ponent walk flat along the waterfront to the foot of the Costa de ses Voltes, then climb about 100 steps to the old town; about 15 minutes in all. A public lift at the Costa de ses Voltes rises 25 m to the Claustre del Carme viewpoint, but it has had repeated breakdowns, so be ready to use the steps. Many people take the lift up and the steps down. If your ship is at the Cos Nou, allow about 20 minutes.

transportSections.time: About 15 min to the old town
transportSections.detail: Costa de ses Voltes is a wide stone staircase below the old walls. The lift beside it (opened 2021) connects the port with the Claustre del Carme viewpoint and market. Allow extra time for queues at the lift when several ships are in.

transportSections.time: About 15 min to Binibeca or Punta Prima; 45–50 min to Ciutadella
transportSections.detail: Taxis wait at the cruise terminal. Book or agree the return trip in advance for longer journeys.

transportSections.cost: Pay cash to the driver; small notes
transportSections.detail: The Maó bus station is about 10 minutes' walk from the old town. Route 92 runs to Sant Lluís and Punta Prima and route 24 to Sa Mesquida, both seasonal; route 2 goes to Es Castell; routes 1 and 14 go to Ciutadella. Timetables change often and services are reduced outside summer, so check the TIB timetable for your date.
Glass-bottomed harbour tours from Moll de Llevant 12, with departures listed at 10:30, 12:00, 13:30, 15:00 and 16:30. A good way to see the Lazareto and the Isla del Rey without a long trip.

returnTiming.rule: Be back at the ship 60 minutes before all-aboard: 16:30 for a 17:30 all-aboard. From Ciutadella, leave so you are back in Maó at least 90 minutes before.
returnTiming.detail: Start down from the old town in good time: the lift can queue when several ships are in, and it has broken down before, so the steps are the reliable route. Ciutadella is about 45 km away, 45–50 minutes by road, and summer traffic or a missed bus leaves little margin.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If the lift is out of service, walk down the Costa de ses Voltes steps, about 10 minutes. From beaches or Ciutadella, take a taxi straight to the Moll de Ponent. If you will miss all-aboard, call the port agent number on your daily programme straight away.

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: Walk or lift up from the quay; Museu de Menorca €4, free on Sundays (2026)

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: TIB bus routes 1 or 14, or taxi, 45–50 min each way
diyVsExcursion.saving: Worth it alone only on a long call

excursionAdvice: Skip the ship's tour for Maó: the old town starts at the top of the steps and the harbour boats leave from the waterfront. A ship's tour makes sense for Ciutadella on a short call, because it is 45 km away and buses and summer traffic make an independent return tight, and for island tours that string together prehistoric sites and villages you cannot easily link by bus. For a beach, a taxi to Punta Prima or Binibeca is simple to do yourself.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at 08:00 at the Moll de Ponent and all-aboard is 17:30.

steps.what: Walk off the ship along the waterfront and take the lift or the Costa de ses Voltes steps up to the old town.
Coffee in Plaça de la Conquesta, then walk to Santa Maria church.
Museu de Menorca in the former Franciscan convent (opens 10:00, closed Mondays): prehistoric to British-period collections.
Mercat del Claustre in the cloister of the Carme church, then the Mercat de Peix next door.
Standing lunch of tapas, Mahón cheese and sobrassada at the Mercat de Peix stalls.
Walk down to the harbour. One-hour Yellow Catamarans harbour trip from Moll de Llevant, or a taxi to Punta Prima for a swim.
Back on the waterfront. Visit the Xoriguer gin distillery shop on the Moll de Ponent.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Santa Maria church
sights.why: Menorca's best-known church, 18th century, with 17 side chapels and a large pipe organ.
sights.tip: Short organ recitals are held around midday on most days except Sunday; check the time at the door.

sights.name: Museu de Menorca
sights.why: The island's main museum, in a former Franciscan convent, covering prehistoric, Roman, Moorish and British Menorca.
sights.tip: Open 10:00–19:00 Tuesday and Thursday, 10:00–14:00 Wednesday and Friday to Sunday; closed Mondays.

sights.name: Mercat del Claustre and Mercat de Peix
sights.why: A food market in the cloister of the Carme church, and the 1920s fish market next to it, with tapas and wine stalls.
sights.tip: The lift from the port comes out right by the Claustre del Carme, so this is an easy first or last stop.

sights.name: Mahón harbour by boat
sights.why: Often described as the largest and deepest natural harbour in the Mediterranean, with the Lazareto and the old British naval hospital on the Isla del Rey.
sights.tip: Glass-bottomed boats leave from Moll de Llevant 12.

sights.name: Xoriguer gin distillery
sights.why: Menorca's gin, a legacy of the British period, made and sold on the Moll de Ponent beside the cruise quay.
sights.tip: Try a pomada, gin with lemonade, the island's summer drink.

sights.name: Ca n'Oliver (Hernández Sanz Centre of Art and History)
sights.why: A 19th-century town mansion with an imperial staircase and collections on Maó's history.
sights.tip: A good indoor stop on a hot or wet afternoon.

sights.name: Teatre Principal
sights.why: The oldest opera house in Spain, opened in 1829.
sights.tip: Combine with a walk past the Georgian-style houses of the British era.

sights.name: Isla del Rey
sights.why: Harbour island with an 18th-century British naval hospital and, since 2021, a Hauser & Wirth art gallery.
sights.cost: Check boat and gallery details before you go
sights.tip: Reached by boat; check return times so you are back at the quay in time.

beaches.name: Punta Prima
beaches.howToGetThere: Taxi, or seasonal TIB route 92 from the Maó bus station
beaches.time: About 15 min by taxi; about 10 km
beaches.note: Sandy beach on the south-east coast with restaurants overlooking the sea.

beaches.name: Binibeca (Binibèquer)
beaches.note: Beach and the whitewashed village of Binibeca Vell; the village is residential, so keep noise down.

food.dish: Tapas, Mahón cheese and Menorcan wine
food.where: Mercat de Peix, Plaça del Carme 5
Xoriguer distillery shop, Moll de Ponent, and harbour bars
Restaurants along the Moll de Llevant and Moll de Ponent
Fornells, on the north coast (a long call or a tour)

commonMistakes.mistake: Relying on the lift for the return.
commonMistakes.fix: It has broken down repeatedly since 2021 and queues when several ships are in. Know the Costa de ses Voltes steps, about 10 minutes down.

commonMistakes.mistake: Visiting the Museu de Menorca on a Monday or in the afternoon.
commonMistakes.fix: It is closed on Mondays and shuts at 14:00 except on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

commonMistakes.mistake: Shopping in the old town after lunch.
commonMistakes.fix: Many shops close roughly 13:30–16:30. Shop in the morning or on the waterfront.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying Ciutadella on a short call by bus.
commonMistakes.fix: It is 45 km and 45–50 minutes each way. Go only on a long call, or with a tour.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming the beach buses run every day of the year.
commonMistakes.fix: Routes 92 and 24 are seasonal and timetables change often. Check TIB, or take a taxi.

safety: Maó is a quiet, safe town. The main hazards are the steep steps from the port in summer heat, and traffic on the harbour road where coaches and taxis pick up. Carry water for the climb. Swim only where flags show it is safe and away from the busy harbour.
accessibility: The quayside and waterfront are flat. The old town is about 25–30 m higher; step-free access depends on the public lift at the Costa de ses Voltes, which rises 25 m to the Claustre del Carme viewpoint but has had several breakdowns, so ask on board whether it is working. A taxi from the cruise terminal is the alternative. Inside the old town the streets are compact, with some slopes.
rainyDay: Spend the morning in the Museu de Menorca and Ca n'Oliver, then the covered Mercat del Claustre and Mercat de Peix for lunch, and Santa Maria church for the organ. A harbour boat trip still works in light rain; beaches do not.
crowdTips: The port can take three cruise ships at once, and the lift and the top of the steps get busy when passengers come ashore together. Go up straight away and visit the markets and museum in the morning, when shops and museums are also open. Return early on multi-ship days to avoid the lift queue.

faqs.a: No for most ships. Cruise ships dock on the Moll de Ponent below the old town; some smaller ships use other quays such as the Cos Nou.

faqs.q: Is Mahón walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes. The old town is about 650 m and 15 minutes away, up 100-plus steps or by the public lift.

faqs.q: Is there a lift from Mahón port to the town?
faqs.a: Yes. A lift at the Costa de ses Voltes, opened in 2021, rises 25 m to the Claustre del Carme. It has had breakdowns, so be ready to use the steps.

faqs.q: What can I do in Mahón in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Santa Maria church, the Museu de Menorca, the Claustre and fish markets, a one-hour harbour boat trip and a pomada at the Xoriguer distillery, or a swim at Punta Prima.
Punta Prima and Binibeca are about 10 km and 15 minutes by taxi. Sa Mesquida is about 6 km north. Buses run in season.

faqs.q: Can I visit Ciutadella from Mahón cruise port?
faqs.a: On a long call. It is 45 km and 45–50 minutes by bus or taxi each way; leave enough time to be back 90 minutes before all-aboard.
Yes. Take care on the steep steps in heat and on the harbour road.
